To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined optimal immunohistochemical protocols for the examination of mouse and human macrophage markers in formalin fixed parrafined embedded tissue sections.
we developed optimal immunohistochemical protocols and storage procedures for macrophage staining using various antibodies in FFPE tissue sections.

the optimal immunohistochemical procedure for staining macrophages with various antibodies in formalin-fixed paraffin- embedded tissue samples is heat treatment with ethylene-diamine-tetraacetic acid (EDTA) solution, pH 6.0, or EDTA solution, pH 9.0, followed by storage at -80°C in a deep freezer for 3 months.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an optimum IHC protocol for macrophage staining in FFPE tissue samples.
the optimization of IHC protocols for macrophage staining and the establishment of storage procedures for FFPE sections.
the establishment of optimum IHC procedures for macrophages in FFPE samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best IHC protocol for macrophage staining in FFPE samples depends on the primary antibody and the species of origin (human or mouse).
the best antigen retrieval method for IHC of mouse and human macrophages in FFPE samples is heat treatment with ethylene diamine tetra acetic acid (EDTA) solution at pH 8.5.
the most appropriate IHC protocol for macrophage analysis in FFPE samples is the combination of heat treatment with EDTA, pH 8, and a 3% hydrogen peroxide solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal protocols and storage procedures for the examination of mouse macrophages were the same as those for human macrophages, and that the immunoreactivities of macrophages were preserved in storage at −80°C.
IHC of FFPE samples is a useful tool for examination and analysis of macrophage phenotypes, and the optimum IHC protocol should be determined for the antibody used.

heat treatment with EDTA solution, pH 9.0, is a useful antigen retrieval protocol for staining of macro phages with a range antibodies in FFPE tissue samples, and that storage of sliced FFPE samples at -80 ° C is an appropriate method for preservation of immunoreactivities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal combination of antibody and antigen retrieval method is required for IHC of macrophages.
the immunoreactivities of sliced tissue sections gradually decrease over time in long-term storage at room temperature.
the combination of primary antibodies and the antigen retrieval methods are important factors in the evaluation of macrophages by IHC.
